title: The Shadow
narration: In 2019, we saw a black hole's shadow for the first time. M87* weighs 6.5 billion suns. But why does its edge exist? The answer lies in a vanishing point.
visual_goal: Show the iconic orange ring of M87* against darkness, then zoom into the center where light disappears.

title: The Point of No Return
narration: At the event horizon, escape velocity hits 299,792,458 meters per second—light speed. Beyond this 0.08 AU sphere around Sagittarius A*, space itself ends. Nothing comes back.
visual_goal: Animate the spherical boundary around the Milky Way's core, showing light rays bending and being trapped.

title: The Ripples
narration: In 2015, LIGO heard two black holes collide. Their combined 62 solar masses rang spacetime like a bell. We've detected over 90 mergers since. These waves are echoes of swallowed stars.
visual_goal: Visualize gravitational waves as ripples distorting a grid of stars, then show two spiraling masses merging.

title: The Temperature of Nothing
narration: Hawking radiation gives a solar-mass hole a temperature of 0.00000006 kelvins. It will evaporate in 1.5×10^67 years. The universe will be unrecognizable by then. Black holes are not forever.
visual_goal: Show a faint glow around a black hole against a cold, starless background, with time-lapse of stars dying around it.
search_queries: cold empty space black hole glow

title: The Unseen Mass
narration: A hundred million black holes drift through the Milky Way. We've imaged two. Sagittarius A*, 26,960 light-years away, holds our galaxy together. Where space ends, mystery begins.
visual_goal: Pan across the Milky Way's star field, highlighting faint black hole candidates, then settle on the Sagittarius A* image from 2022.
